title: Exactly-once with checkpoint barriers
description: A streaming job counts payments per merchant and writes to Kafka. Walk through one checkpoint that makes its output exactly-once.

problemStatement.overview:
A Flink-style job reads payment events from Kafka, keeps a running total per merchant, and writes the totals to another Kafka topic. Machines will fail, and when they do the job replays from its last checkpoint.

Exactly-once doesn't mean each event is physically processed once. It means the state and the output look as if it was. That takes three things lined up: a consistent snapshot of source offsets and operator state, taken without stopping the job, and a sink that only publishes output once the snapshot is safe.

The outline covers one checkpoint. Fill the blocks. Traps either duplicate output or stop the world.
problemStatement.yourTask: Order the steps of one checkpoint, from injecting the barrier to the sink making results visible.
yourTaskSteps: Fill each empty block from Unused.
hints: Barriers travel in the data stream itself and never overtake records.
Output must not become visible until the whole checkpoint is complete.
Replaying input is fine if the state and output roll back to the same point.
problemStatement.moat:
Setter notes, not shown to learners.

Required chain: inject-barrier → barrier-flows → snapshot-state → sink-precommit → checkpoint-complete → sink-commit.
Optional splice: align-inputs on barrier-flows → snapshot-state.
Five traps.

platformSpec.passMessage: Barrier, snapshot, pre-commit, complete, commit. Replays now produce the same output.

pieces.title: Inject checkpoint barrier n at the sources
pieces.blurb: The coordinator tells each source to record its Kafka offsets and emit barrier n into its output stream.

pieces.title: Barrier flows downstream with the records
pieces.blurb: The barrier travels in-band. Records before it belong to checkpoint n; records after it belong to n+1.

pieces.title: Align barriers across inputs
pieces.blurb: An operator with several inputs holds back inputs whose barrier already arrived until the rest catch up. Unaligned checkpoints skip this by also saving in-flight records.

pieces.title: Snapshot operator state, forward the barrier
pieces.blurb: Each operator writes its per-merchant totals to durable storage asynchronously, then passes the barrier on.

pieces.title: Sink pre-commits its transaction
pieces.blurb: When the barrier reaches the sink, it flushes its open Kafka transaction but does not commit it. Readers using read_committed can't see it yet.

pieces.title: Every task acknowledges: checkpoint complete
pieces.blurb: The coordinator has acknowledgements from all tasks, so checkpoint n is durable and becomes the restore point.

pieces.title: Sink commits; output becomes visible
pieces.blurb: Notified that the checkpoint is complete, the sink commits the Kafka transaction. Downstream consumers now see the totals.

pieces.title: Pause the whole job for the snapshot
pieces.blurb: Stop all sources, wait for in-flight records to drain, snapshot everything, then resume.
pieces.trapIfPlaced: Barriers exist so the job never has to stop. Snapshots happen while records keep flowing.

pieces.title: Commit Kafka offsets after every record
pieces.blurb: Committing the consumer offset after each event guarantees nothing is processed twice.
pieces.trapIfPlaced: Offsets alone don't cover operator state or sink output. A crash between them still duplicates or loses data.

pieces.title: Sink writes immediately, no transaction
pieces.blurb: Each total is produced to the output topic as soon as it's computed. Replays just write the same thing again.
pieces.trapIfPlaced: Running totals aren't idempotent writes. On replay, consumers see duplicate or out-of-date totals.

pieces.title: Sink commits after its own snapshot
pieces.blurb: As soon as the sink has snapshotted its state, it commits the transaction without waiting for anyone else.
pieces.trapIfPlaced: If another task fails, the job rolls back to checkpoint n-1, but this output is already visible.

pieces.title: Each event is processed exactly once
pieces.blurb: Exactly-once means the engine guarantees no event ever passes through an operator twice.
pieces.trapIfPlaced: Events can be reprocessed after a failure. Exactly-once is about the effect on state and output.
